title: Spatio-Temporal Trajectory Similarity Learning in Road Networks

problem.claim: Trajectory similarity computation needs to support time-aware analyses in road networks.

gap.claim: Existing learning-based solutions prioritize spatial similarity over temporal similarity, limiting their suitability for time-aware analyses.

contributions.claim: ST2Vec is a representation-learning solution for spatio-temporal trajectory similarity computation in road networks.

ST2Vec models fine-grained spatial and temporal relations, uses a generic temporal modeling module, and applies spatio-temporal co-attention fusion with two fusion strategies to generate unified trajectory embeddings.
ST2Vec uses curriculum learning under triplet loss to improve model optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their generic temporal modeling module is proposed for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The experimental study reports that ST2Vec substantially outperforms state-of-the-art competitors in effectiveness and efficiency.
The authors report low parameter sensitivity and good model robustness.
Case studies on top-k querying and DBSCAN clustering provide additional insight into ST2Vec's capabilities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning may improve the efficiency and adaptability of trajectory similarity computation.
Existing learning-based approaches emphasize spatial similarity and underrepresent temporal similarity.
ST2Vec is introduced to compute spatio-temporal similarity by learning fine-grained spatial and temporal trajectory relations.
The method combines spatial-temporal modeling, co-attention fusion, and curriculum learning with triplet loss.
Experiments and case studies report strong effectiveness, efficiency, robustness, and applicability to querying and clustering.

source_observation.claim: Curriculum learning is used during optimization under triplet loss, and the authors report improved convergence and effectiveness.

interpretation.claim: Structured training-example progression may help optimize representation-learning objectives for similarity tasks.

application.claim: Consider curriculum-based optimization when training similarity representations with triplet loss.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the curriculum design, comparison conditions, or which datasets benefit most.
